For this exercise, you should create the R code needed to make a dot map of thefts from vehicles in Vancouver in 2020. 

## Before you start

Complete Chapters 1–5 of [_Learn Crime Mapping with R_](https://books.lesscrime.info/learncrimemapping/).

In this exercise you will practise downloading and reading data, filtering rows, converting coordinates into a spatial object, and creating a point map. The coordinate-system codes needed for this dataset are supplied below.


### What your map should show

Your map should show offences in the category 'Theft from Vehicle' that occurred in Vancouver in 2020. You can download the data from:

```
https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/vancouver_thefts.csv.gz
```

See the [dataset documentation](https://pkgs.lesscrime.info/crimemappingdata/reference/vancouver_thefts.html) for the columns and source. The `X` and `Y` columns use the UTM zone 10 north coordinate reference system (EPSG:32610), and the address column is anonymised to the nearest 100 block.

Your map should include: 

  1. a layer showing (as points) the locations of individual thefts from vehicles,
  2. a suitable base map.

Every step of your code should be accompanied by an explanatory comment (on one or more lines starting with a `#` symbol and a space). Your code should only produce a map (and possibly some R messages or warnings), not output anything else (e.g. a copy of the data).


### Checklist for this exercise

Use this checklist to make sure you have done everything required for this exercise.


#### The map

- The map shows the locations of individual crimes.
- The points use a colour that stands out from the background.
- You have made design choices that make it as easy as possible to show where thefts from vehicles are most concentrated.


#### The code

- There is no temporary code – e.g. `head()` – in your script file.
- The code loads the necessary packages _at the start of the script_ in a single call to the `pacman::p_load()` function.
- The code uses `request()` and `req_perform()` to download the data to a local file in the `data/raw` folder.
- The code uses `here()` to specify file paths within your workspace.
- The code loads the downloaded local file into R.
- The code converts all the column names in the data to `snake_case` and only uses snake-case object names.
- The code converts the data to an SF object.
- The code filters the data to only include the type of crime you are interested in.
- The code uses the pipe operator `|>` to link together functions into a data-wrangling pipeline.


### Check your answer

After attempting the task, you can read this [specimen answer and explanation](vancouver_vehicle_thefts_answer.qmd) to get an idea of what a potential solution looks like.
